title: Notification service with failover
idea: The core implementation is one `NotificationService` that dedupes by idempotency key, checks preferences, then walks an ordered provider list with bounded retries until one provider accepts.

analogy.text: Calling a support line. You dial a busy number twice, then try the backup number. A wrong number means you stop dialling altogether.
analogy.breaks: A phone call has no idempotency key; a redial is a new call.

points: The idempotency key is checked first, so a replay returns the stored result.
An opt-out ends the flow as SKIPPED before any provider is called.
RETRYABLE retries the same provider, then fails over to the next one.
REJECTED means the request itself is bad, so failover would not help.

steps.caption: A caller sends request `k1`: an OTP by SMS for U-1.
The key `k1` is new, so the service creates N-1 and stores it.
U-1 has not muted SMS, so the request continues.
sms-a answers RETRYABLE twice. Each provider gets two tries in total.
The service fails over to sms-b, which accepts on the first try.
N-1 returns as SENT, with all three attempts recorded.
The caller retries `k1` after a timeout. Dedupe returns N-1; no provider is called.

code.title: Retry and failover
code.caption: The full send algorithm, single-threaded for now. `Provider.send` now returns a `Result`, not a boolean, so the service can tell retry from reject. Notification is trimmed to id, status and attempts.

walk.text: sms-a fails twice, sms-b never fails. U-2 has muted email.
Four requests: a fresh OTP, its replay, a muted email, and a bad number.
Providers per channel in failover order, tries per provider, preferences, and the key map.
A known key returns the stored Notification. A new key gets the next id.
An opt-out is recorded as SKIPPED, so callers can tell it from a failure.
Try each provider up to its budget. OK wins; REJECTED stops everything.
Every provider ran out of tries: the notification is FAILED.

pitfalls: Never fail over on REJECTED; a bad phone number fails at every vendor.
Store the key before calling providers, or a retry during a slow send sends twice.
Add a backoff between retries in production; hammering a struggling provider makes it worse.

quiz.q: What does the last line of NotificationCore print?
quiz.why: N-1 calls sms-a twice and sms-b once. The replay calls nobody. The bad number calls sms-a once and stops: 3 and 1.

takeaway: Dedupe first, retry a bounded number of times, then fail over.

starters: How do I classify a provider error as RETRYABLE or REJECTED?
Should a failed SMS fall back to email for the same user?
Where should backoff between retries live in this design?
